?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:27315
Court No. - 76

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 38270 of 2023
Applicant :- Vipin

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Deepak Kumar Pal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Deepak Kumar Pal, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record..

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 129 of 2023, under sections 498-A, 306, 504 I.P.C., Police Station Mandawar, District Bijnor,
during pendency of the trial.

3. F.I.R. of the present case was lodged against the applicant under section 498A, 504, 304B I.P.C.
and 3/4 D.P. Act and according to the F.I.R. marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased on 09.03.2019 and after marriage applicant tortured his wife for want of dowry and on 23.04.2023 he committed the murder of the deceased by administering some poisonous substance.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is husband of the deceased and he never tortured his wife and allegation of torture and demand of dowry was found false during investigation and after investigation charge sheet was filed only under sections 498A, 306,504 I.P.C.

sentences.text: He further submits that however before death dying declaration of the deceased was recorded but she did not make any allegation of torture and only stated that she was having only two female child and she is not having any say in the family, therefore, in anger she consumed sulphas medicines.
5. He further submits that even from the dying declaration it could not be reflected that due to the abetment of the applicant deceased committed suicide.

He further submits that even after consumption of the poisonous substance applicant admitted the deceased in the hospital and this fact is evident from parcha of the case diary which has been annexed at page no. 26 of the affidavit.
He further submits that the applicant is not having any criminal history and is in jail since 27.04.2023 i.e. for more than 9 months.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail and submits that applicant is husband of the deceased and even from the dying declaration of the deceased it reflects that she was not being properly treated by the applicant and his family members only due to the reason that she was not having any male child and, therefore, it cannot be said that there is no abetment on the part of applicant.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. However, applicant is husband of the deceased but it appears that during investigation the dying declaration of the deceased was recorded and as per the dying declaration as deceased was having only female child, therefore, she was not having any say in the family and in anger she consumed poisonous substance.

Therefore, this Court finds force in the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that at this stage it cannot be said that due to the abetment of the applicant deceased committed suicide.
Further, applicant is not having criminal history and he is in jail since 27.04.2023.

9. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is also entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant -Vipin be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

Vipin vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164597736/
2 (iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
